body_text:
The *dual space* $V^* = \operatorname{Hom}_F(V, F) = \mathcal{L}(V, F)$ is
the vector space of all linear functionals $\varphi : V \to F$.

If $\mathcal{B} = (b_1, \dots, b_n)$ is a basis of $V$, its *dual basis*
$\mathcal{B}^* = (b^1, \dots, b^n)$ of $V^*$ is uniquely determined by:
$$ b^i(b_j) = \delta_{ij} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } i = j, \\ 0 & \text{if } i \neq j. \end{cases} $$
The functional $b^i$ extracts the $i$-th coordinate of a vector relative to $\mathcal{B}$.

For finite-dimensional spaces, $\dim(V^*) = \dim(V)$, so $V \cong V^*$.
Furthermore, the evaluation map $\operatorname{ev} : V \to V^{**}$ into the
double dual (bidual), defined by $\operatorname{ev}(v)(\varphi) = \varphi(v)$,
is a *canonical* (basis-independent) isomorphism when $\dim(V) < \infty$,
rendering finite-dimensional vector spaces reflexive.
